feedback.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}a+3b=-6 \\ \frac{5}{3}a-\frac{1}{3}b=9\end{aligned}
$$

$a=$
{{field-1}}$,\,b=$
{{field-2}}
feedback.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second equation by $3,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}a+3b=-6 & |\times 2 \\ \frac{5}{3}a-\frac{1}{3}b=9 & |\times 3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}-5a+6b=-12 \\ 5a-b=27\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $a$ by adding the two equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{5a}+6b & =-12 \\ \cancel{5a}-b & =27 \\ (6b-b) & =(-12+27) \\ 5b & =15 \\ b & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $b=3$ into the second equation to solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5a-b & =27 \\ 5a-3 & =27 \\ 5a & =30 \\ a & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $a=6,\,b=3.$
